parallel.requirements: The parallel parent understood the need for byte-exact CLI output, no newline, glibc-like atoi behavior, Rust 2021, no external crates, and a complete /output Cargo project.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It delegated a seven-phase workflow: four spec reconstructions, one synthesis, three implementations, judging, assembly, verification, repair, and final reporting; the first four spec agents blocked all later stages.
parallel.implementation: No final Rust implementation reached /output. The parent created a scratch Python oracle in /tmp and some children probed or prototyped, but the workflow never reached implementation or assembly.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow state ended killed with result null, final.txt was empty, artifact validation found no files, and the required test2.rs deliverable was absent from the captured artifact.
parallel.verification: The parent and children probed the C++ executable, but no integrated Rust deliverable was built or tested by the completed parallel run before evaluation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed against an empty or missing artifact and passed 0/40; the task was unfinished because the Spec retry loop consumed the run window.

serial.requirements: The serial run identified the same byte-exact output, no-dependency Rust 2021, /output/test2.rs, Cargo project, black-box, and reference-binary obligations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor retained ownership of probing, implementation, packaging, testing, and final response, with no delegation or workflow subagents.
serial.implementation: It wrote cstdlib.rs plus earcut modules for point, node, geometry, triangulate, tests, and mod wiring, then created Cargo.toml and test2.rs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It built both a standalone /output/test2 and Cargo release binary, leaving a populated artifact tree with the expected root entry file.
serial.verification: It ran byte-exact comparisons against the C++ binary, cargo tests, release build, and a final matrix showing 104/104 output matches and matching exits/stderr.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No evaluator-visible defect remained; the final note disclosed a non-UTF-8 argv caveat, but the official completed evaluation passed 40/40.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the exact output, atoi, dependency, Rust edition, and /output requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirements and validated them with reference-binary probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no material task-requirement recognition gap; the divergence came after recognition, in lifecycle and delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run chose a staged workflow with four spec agents first and later synthesis, implementation, judging, assembly, verification, and repair stages.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept all ownership in the parent and proceeded directly from probing to file creation, build, tests, fixes, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ownership was gated through a workflow that never escaped the first delegated phase; serial ownership stayed continuous and moved into implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child retries received the same broad original task preview rather than a checkpoint carrying prior probe findings or partial spec progress.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept reference-output, toolchain, and implementation findings in one uninterrupted context and used them in subsequent edits.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost usable state across retry boundaries; serial had no cross-agent or retry boundary where findings had to be transferred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel never reached a completed implementation phase and left /output without project files in the artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the Rust modules, entry point, Cargo manifest, tests, and compiled executable directly in /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial path produced and revised concrete Rust files; the parallel path stayed in probing/spec work and did not install a deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow result was null and the workflow state was killed; many child attempts ended with interruption instead of a returned structured result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial result lifecycle completed: build outputs were generated, checked, and summarized in a final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not retrieve or promote workflow outputs because none completed the staged pipeline; serial carried results through to final delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no final-tree collision or merge, but also no installed /output project; artifact validation listed no files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all source files into one Cargo project and artifact validation lists test2.rs, Cargo files, modules, and binaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The difference is absence of integration in parallel, not a conflicting shared-state merge; serial integrated and packaged the project.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel probed the reference binary but had no completed integrated Rust artifact to build, diff-test, or accept before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran unit tests, release build, standalone rustc build, and a 104/104 byte-exact differential matrix before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was evaluator-aligned and post-build; parallel verification remained preliminary and never accepted a final product.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full cell window with return code 143, a killed workflow, 23 child logs, and no artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally with return code 0, remaining budget, final response, and an evaluator-passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was timeout-driven after retry churn; serial closure followed successful build and verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is serial_only_pass: the current completed status records parallel 0/40 and serial 40/40. The concrete task-solving difference is not that the serial run had an easier task; both prompts match. Serial kept responsibility local, built the required files, verified byte-exact behavior, and delivered a valid artifact. Parallel delegated the first phase to four spec children, repeatedly retried stalled children without carrying forward prior progress, never reached implementation/assembly, timed out, and left the evaluator with no files.
parallel_contributors: Repeated checkpoint-free retries of stalled Spec children consumed the workflow window before implementation or assembly.
The final artifact validation found no files, so the official evaluator had no usable Rust project to test.
serial_contributors: Single-context ownership preserved findings and moved directly into writing and fixing /output files.
Serial verification ran a 104/104 byte-exact matrix and the official evaluator passed 40/40.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The parallel run has no final implementation to compare for ordinary algorithmic defects.
The serial run corrected an internal atoi test expectation before final verification.

candidates.reason: The workflow had planned implementation owners in its Implement phase; implementation was not reached because the Spec retry loop consumed the run, not because no implementer was assigned.
No separately completed components required integration, and the script later assigns Judge and Assemble work; the concrete failure occurred earlier.
The workflow explicitly includes an Assemble phase responsible for installing the winning implementation into /output; it was not reached.
The generated workflow owned the end-to-end pipeline across phases; the problem was stalled checkpoint-free retries within the first phase.
The gate was not one mandatory serial preflight; it was a multi-child spec phase with repeated retries and no checkpoint inheritance.
The investigation phase did not complete and then squeeze later work; it repeatedly restarted and stalled before synthesis or implementation.
Implementation was starved, but only as the downstream effect of the same checkpoint-free Spec retry chain, so the context boundary is more specific.
Fan-out and budget exhaustion are visible, but they are the same episode as the checkpoint-free retry loop; the retained label captures the directly correctable boundary.
No single child assignment is the independent overbroad unit relative to sibling work; all four spec roles were retried in the same stalled workflow chain.
The child prompts carried the task source, hard rules, reference-output table, and delivery expectations; the problem was retry state loss, not an omitted initial requirement.
No independently produced implementations reached a point where incompatible file names, APIs, or component interfaces had to be reconciled.
The key loss occurred at retry boundaries before a completed handoff; no completed transfer is shown omitting a known finding to a receiver.
No large completed child handoff reached the parent and was left unconsumed because of size or structure.
No receiver is shown acting on a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state after a completed handoff.
The workflow never gathered incompatible completed reports that the parent then failed to adjudicate.
The parallel final response is empty and the workflow was killed; the parent did not present an unsupported whole-task completion claim.

Replacement attempts for the same Spec roles restarted from the original broad task prompt, while earlier attempts had already probed and even validated useful findings; the loop consumed budget and still produced no required output.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow spent the available run window repeatedly restarting spec work, never reached implementation or assembly, and left no artifact files for evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out and timeout pressure were visible, but the repeated no-checkpoint replacement boundary is more specific than treating the same chain as generic budget exhaustion.
